A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transfer attack. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original evasion-rate and image-perturbation experiments, comparisons with existing attacks, sensitivity studies and ablations in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds SSIM-constrained comparisons, computational measurements and empirical independence tests, including Table 2 and Figures 11 and 14.

M1.justification: The bootstrapped surrogate models, watermark-selection options, aggregation variants and projected-gradient optimization remain unchanged. Equations 1–3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same objective, projection and stopping procedure.

E1.justification: Stable Diffusion and Midjourney remain the target-image sources, with DALL-E 2 supplying surrogate training images. The image-watermark evasion task is retained. Added watermarking models extend robustness comparisons within this coverage without introducing a new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: The attack comparisons retain WEvade-B-S, AdvEmb-RN18, AdvCls-Real&WM, AdvCls-Enc-WM1&WM2, MI-CWA and DiffPure, alongside the same four post-processing methods. The new SSIM and timing comparisons use existing comparators; RingID and Gaussian Shading are target watermarking systems.

E3.justification: Figure 11 adds an SSIM-constraint sweep from 1.00 to 0.60 for the 30-bit ResNet target on Stable Diffusion. The earlier JPEG/DWT-DCT and Gaussian-noise/Tree-Ring comparison is replaced by a common Gaussian-noise sweep over Tree-Ring, RingID, Gaussian Shading and HiDDeN. Table 2 adds a single-GPU timing comparison. Core experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds focused analyses of performance across SSIM budgets, surrogate-output independence and computational cost, and revises the non-learning watermark robustness comparison. Existing surrogate-count, sensitivity, aggregation-variant and theoretical-versus-empirical analyses are retained, sometimes merged or relocated.

E5.justification: Figure 14 newly reports chi-square independence tests at stated 0.95 confidence: 100 randomly sampled surrogate-model pairs are tested separately for each bit using 1,000 perturbed images. This adds statistical testing; it does not document additional independent runs of the main attack experiments.

E6.justification: Retained attack-result plots are unchanged. New results include SSIM-dependent evasion curves, approximately 85–93% independence-test pass rates per bit, and computational costs; Table 2 reports 6.50 training hours and 177.97 seconds per image for the proposed attack. Figure 6c replaces the earlier non-learning post-processing comparison with an expanded Gaussian-noise comparison.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, lemmas, bounds and proofs retain their mathematical substance. v3's Theorem 3 becomes v4's Theorem 1, while supporting material is reorganized into Appendices B–G. The new independence test supplies empirical analysis without changing the formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify the vulnerability claim as applying to existing watermarking methods. The introduction now explicitly states that effectiveness against a completely new target method is unclear. The principal methodological, theoretical and empirical contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds explicit limitations concerning entirely different target methods, computational expense and potentially greater costs for high-capacity watermarks. It discusses parallelization and one-time training as mitigations. New Appendix A discusses misuse and tentatively proposes fundamentally different, confidential watermarking mechanisms as a defense.

D1.justification: v4 adds an authors' code-access link in the abstract and training/inference measurements on an NVIDIA RTX-6000 GPU in Table 2. Existing dataset processing, architecture descriptions, hyperparameters and pseudocode are largely retained, with experimental details moved into Appendices H–L.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Zhao, Saberi and Lukas on watermark attacks, RingID and Gaussian Shading, and Zhong and Shih on high-capacity watermarking. It removes the standalone Invisible watermark reference. These broaden context without substantially changing the positioning of the surrogate-watermark ensemble contribution.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and condensed. Most theoretical development moves from Section 5 into Appendix B, formal definitions are integrated there, and detailed experimental descriptions move into Appendices H–L. Ethics and acknowledgment sections are added, alongside author-year citations and conference-header changes.

P2.justification: The conference layout substantially changes typography and display density. v3 Figures 5–6 merge into v4 Figure 5; sensitivity and variant plots are combined and relocated into Figures 12–13. v4 also adds Table 2 and Figures 11 and 14, and replaces the old robustness plot with Figure 6c.

improvement.justification: v4 improves transparency through explicit applicability and computational limitations, code-access information and measured costs. Figure 11 strengthens comparison across image-quality budgets while preserving the core evidence. The gains are limited: the method and theory are unchanged, and Figure 14's pairwise tests provide only partial support for the full independence assumption. Extensive presentation changes do not establish a larger scientific improvement.
